Hi Lauren / Marta,

We're starting the internal procurement conversation for a dedicated inference pilot for ArgoHealth. A few numbers from our side: average conversational session ~1,200 tokens, expected steady sessions 40 req/s across the US daytime peak (12:00-18:00 PT), occasional spikes to ~120 req/s for 5-10 minutes, and target p95 generation latency <= 450ms.

Questions: can you give us a ballpark committed slab estimate (GPUs / slabs) to meet the steady-state and spikes with a 1.5x headroom requirement? We also need latency tradeoffs for a quantized 8-bit variant vs a baseline fp16.

Thanks — want to bring solid numbers to procurement next week.

Joe Sullivan

Joe — thanks, this is helpful. I put together a quick back-of-envelope based on the numbers you provided and our serving profiles. High-level notes below; I'll loop in Karthik/Priyom/Ben for a formal run and a spreadsheet with scenarios.

Summary (prelim):
- Workload assumptions: 1,200 tokens/session, steady 40 req/s -> ~48k tokens/s steady; peak 120 req/s -> ~144k tokens/s.
- Model variants we bench: redwood-mistral-30B (fp16) and mistral-30B-8q (8-bit).
- Effective sustained tokens/sec per A100-like slab (conservative):
  - fp16 (mistral-30B): ~12k tokens/s per GPU (single-stream, p95 ~380ms at target sequence),
  - 8-bit quantized: ~18k tokens/s per GPU (p95 ~460ms in some long-seq cases).
- Rough committed slab suggestion to cover steady + 1.5x headroom:
  - fp16 baseline: ceil(48k / 12k * 1.5) = ceil(4 * 1.5) = 6 GPUs (~2 slabs of 3 GPUs or 3 slabs depending on SKU),
  - 8-bit: ceil(48k / 18k * 1.5) = ceil(2.67 * 1.5) = 5 GPUs (~2 slabs).
- For peaks (144k tokens/s) we recommend transient burst policy (burst pool / autoscale) rather than committed slabs unless you want to commit to large headroom. If committed slabs must cover spikes, numbers scale: fp16 -> ~18 GPUs, 8-bit -> ~11 GPUs.

Attachments: preliminary workbook (argo_dedicated_calc.xlsx) with the quick math and scenario toggles; SLA_Scenarios_argo.pdf with p95 targets and fallback suggestions.

I'll get the formal throughput model over the next 48 hours with explicit p95 latency curves, token-per-request sensitivity, and cost delta between fp16 and 8-bit.

—Lauren Bishop

Lauren / team / Joe — draft model attached (argoheadroom_calc_v1.xlsx). Key outputs and assumptions below (TL;DR first):

TL;DR: To meet ArgoHealth steady (48k tokens/s) with 1.5x headroom, recommended committed profile: 5x A100-equivalent GPUs if you pick 8-bit quantized model, or 7x A100-equivalent GPUs for fp16 to preserve sub-450ms p95 on typical session lengths. For commit+burst: commit 3 GPUs (8-bit) with a 6-GPU burst pool to cover 99th-percentile short spikes.

Assumptions / bench notes:
- Bench model: redwood-mistral-30B fp16 and mistral-30B-8q tuned build. Numbers are conservative, measured with latency-SLO-aware batching and continuous KV prefix caching enabled.
- Effective sustained throughput (single-stream, multi-request batching averaged over window):
  - fp16: 11.5k toks/s per GPU (256-token context), drops to ~9.8k toks/s at 1200-token sequences due to attention scaling. p95 generation latency at 1200 tokens ~420-460ms depending on batch mixing.
  - 8-bit quant: 16.8k toks/s per GPU (256-token), ~14.6k toks/s at 1200-token sequences. p95 at 1200 tokens ~500-560ms in worst-case long-tail; median lower.
- Prefix caching: with a warm cache and 40% prefix reuse (typical for ArgoHealth conversation flows), effective tokens/sec increases by ~25%. We used both cached and uncached columns in the workbook.

Committed sizing math (steady + 1.5x headroom):
- Steady tokens: 48k toks/s.
- fp16: baseline GPUs needed = 48k / 9.8k = 4.9 -> rounded up to 5; with 1.5x headroom -> 8 GPUs -> recommend 8 (we previously rounded conservatively to 7 in the quick note; workbook uses 8 to include scheduling fragmentation).
- 8-bit: baseline = 48k / 14.6k = 3.29 -> rounded to 4; with 1.5x headroom -> 6 GPUs.

Peak (burst 144k toks/s):
- If committed to cover peaks: fp16 -> ~15 GPUs; 8-bit -> ~10 GPUs.
- We recommend commit+burst hybrid: commit 6 (8-bit) or 8 (fp16) with autoscale burst pool sized to 8-10 GPUs for the short peaks. This balances cost vs procurement comfort.

Latency notes / tradeoffs:
- fp16 keeps p95 inside target for 1200-token sessions when we provision the higher commit (8 GPUs). 8-bit reduces avg cost but will show p95 drift on the worst long-tail requests — mitigations include prefix caching and a small fp16 fallback pool for cold or high-latency requests.

Ops recommendations:
- Warm cache priming during predicted surge windows (run synthetic warmers 10 minutes before peak).
- Autoscale: prefer short autoscale ramp (30–60s) and a pre-warmed burst pool for multi-minute spikes.
- Canary rollouts for quantized model in a 5–10% traffic slice for first 2 weeks and quality monitoring tied to prompt test-set.

Next steps: Priyom — can you add cost delta rows (committed vs burst) and Ben — please draft a one-page slide for procurement showing "commit only" vs "commit+burst" with expected unit-cost per 1M tokens. Joe — if you can confirm expected prefix reuse % and any quiet-hours constraints, we'll finalize tonight.

Attached: argoheadroom_calc_v1.xlsx (detailed per-model sheets, cache/no-cache columns, p95 curves).

—Karthik
